bull_bear.body: Debt prudence policy: Long-term debt <1.5x Net Worth and <1.5x Forward EBITDA; INR 100 Cr parked in liquid mutual funds (current investments); Focus on internal accruals for incremental efficiency capex.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material price volatility (iron ore/coal); Execution risk on 2 Mn ton expansion; Working capital cycle elongation (guided to 25-30 days) as SS mix increases; Geopolitical impacts on energy/logistics (mitigated by captive power/LNG).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident; Emphasizes 'Sambhv hai, toh sab sambhv hai' (If Sambhv exists, everything is possible); Prudent on debt but aggressive on volume/market share targets (10-12% share in MS/SS by 2030).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Inventory accounting method (WIP valued at cost) neutralizes stock profit/loss volatility; DFT technology reduces size-changeover time from 3-4 hours to near-instant, boosting effective capacity by 10-12k ton/month per machine; PLI incentive capped at ~INR 200 Cr or tonnage, providing a 13-15% revenue boost on eligible thin-gauge production.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- FY26 saw the company "successfully raised INR 440 Cr and listed on stock exchanges"; the FY26 cash flow statement shows proceeds from issue of equity shares of INR 4,400 Million against share issue expenses of INR 237 Million.
- Deleveraging: Debt/Equity moved 1.4 (FY23), 0.8 (FY24), 1.1 (FY25), 0.4 (FY26) and Debt/Op. EBITDA 2.4, 2.2, 3.5, 1.3 over the same years; Net Debt/Op. EBITDA was 0.78x for FY26 and 1.00x as on 30th June'26 on an annualised basis.
- Return ratios: ROCE 20, 18, 12, 16 and ROE 34, 25, 12, 18 (%) across FY23-FY26; ROCE is shown at 15.97% for FY26 and 21.92% annualised as on 30th June'26.
- Reinvestment rather than distribution is the pattern shown: FY26 payments for purchase of property, plant and equipment including CWIP were INR 2,615 Million against net cash generated from operating activities of INR 2,158 Million; no dividend is mentioned anywhere in the deck.
- Cash conversion is disclosed as Cash Flow from Operations to Op. EBITDA of 0.56, 0.89, 0.82 and 0.78 for FY23-FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Carbon Steel: ERW pipes/tubes, GP pipes/coils; Stainless Steel: CR coils (200/300 series), expanding to 400 series; Value-add: Co-branding MOUs (10 live) for pipe manufacturing.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising raw material costs and energy prices squeezing non-integrated peers | Sambhv Steel Tubes Ltd | beneficiary | High | Captive power (100% self-sufficiency at Sarora, partial at Kesda) and in-house iron ore/coal sourcing insulate margins; PLI scheme adds 13-15% incentive on high-value SS production. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Deck's core moat claim is a single-location backward-integrated facility at Sarora, Raipur spanning sponge iron to blooms/slabs to HR/CR coils to ERW/GI pipes, described as an "ERW steel pipes and tubes manufacturer that refines steel directly from iron ore instead of making products from aftermarket coils".
- Three facilities in Chhattisgarh: Sarora (Tilda) 379,410 SQM, Kuthrel 107,640 SQM (operationalised in FY2025 for GP coils, GP pipes, SS HRAP coils and SS CR coils) and Kesda 421,600 SQM greenfield with Environmental Clearance received; all described as being in close proximity to key suppliers.
- Raw-material proximity: a Navratna PSU iron ore mine producing "India's highest grade of iron ore" with access to DRCLO grade, and Maharatna PSU coal mines 250 km from Sarora (subsidiary of the largest coal producer in India) with long-term supply agreements in place.
- Distribution reach expanded from 10 states in FY23 to 15 states and 1 UT in FY26, selling to OEMs through distributors (crane, tractor part, cultivator and telecom tower manufacturers) as well as directly to construction/infrastructure companies and government organisations.
- Q1FY27 validation points: product approvals from Engineers India Limited and Chennai Metro Rail Limited, and 18 new MoUs with stainless-steel pipe partners under "Sambhv" co-branding, taking the total MoU count to 28 partners.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Execution status] The Kesda project is tracked work-package by work-package: 132KV line and sub-station ongoing (target Q4FY27), civil work for the technological structure ~90% (power plant), ~30% (steel melting shop), ~80% (hot rolling mill) and ~40% (Kuthrel Unit-II cold rolling mill), with key machinery ordering completed in Q4FY26 across all divisions and testing/commissioning targeted Q4FY27; site photographs are dated July 26, 2026.
- [Standalone scope] Every financial figure in the deck is labelled standalone, yet the cash flow statement shows an investment in subsidiary of INR 652 Million (FY25), a loan given to subsidiary of INR 8 Million and repayment of loan from subsidiary of INR 273 Million (FY26) - so subsidiary economics are outside the presented numbers.
- [Brand spend] Entered IPL branding through cricket bat sponsorship of multiple players including Prabhsimran Singh and Mukul Choudhary, alongside electronic/outdoor/digital/print advertising and trade fair participation.
- [Board depth] Independent directors include a former Executive Director of SAIL and Whole Time Director of NMDC, a retired IAS officer, and a retired SBI Chief General Manager (Lucknow Circle), alongside a promoter team led by Suresh Kumar Goyal (Chairman & MD, 25+ years).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 EBITDA/ton INR 9,500 inflated by Q3 low-cost raw material (iron ore/coal) usage; FY27 guidance INR 7,500-8,000/ton; Power cost savings of INR 60-70 Cr expected from new captive plants; Raw material pass-through estimated at 50-60% of realization hikes.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Volume growth 10-15% in FY27; Margin: EBITDA/ton INR 7,500-8,000 sustainable in FY27 (Q4 peak of 9,500 due to inventory lag); Order Inflow: Strong demand from solar, warehousing, railways; Capex/Commissioning: Kesda Phase 1 (3.6 L ton SS) by Q4FY27; Brownfield SS debottlenecking (1.16 L ton) immediate.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Management cites strong demand visibility from government capex (railways, metros, airports, solar 500GW target) but does not disclose a specific numeric order book value; utilization targets imply healthy fill-rates (SS 60-65%, MS 65-70%, GP 80-90%).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 2 Mn ton finished steel capacity by 2030 (10 L ton MS pipes, 3 L ton coated, 7 L ton SS); Greenfield Kesda project (Phase 1: 3.6 L ton SS); Potential seamless pipe entry under PLI 1.2 pending approvals.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Sambhv Steel delivered a landmark Q4FY26 with PAT doubling to INR 56 Cr and EBITDA/ton peaking at INR 9,500 driven by low-cost raw material inventory and strong realizations. The company is aggressively expanding capacity toward a 2 Mn ton target by 2030, leveraging PLI incentives and captive power to sustain margins despite rising input costs.
